title: AI Ad Adjacency Shield
oneLiner: A media-buying risk workbench that spots when ads or creator partnerships sit too close to AI slop, unsafe context, or off-brand content.
targetUser: Performance marketers, media buyers, creator partnership managers, agencies, and brand-safety leads placing spend across short-form video, newsletters, and creator feeds.
keyUx: Enter campaign, creator/channel list, audience fit, example posts, unsafe keywords, AI-content signals, spend at risk, and approval rules; the app scores suitability, flags risky adjacency, compares creator context, and creates a buy/hold/review decision memo.
externalSignals: Signal 5 — eMarketer — FAQ on brand safety: How AI content and creator marketing are reshaping risk in 2026 — https://www.emarketer.com/content/faq-on-brand-safety--how-ai-content-creator-marketing-reshaping-risk-2026

Signal 6 — Reddit r/technology — Microsoft Satya Nadella wants people to stop saying AI slop in 2026 — https://www.reddit.com/r/technology/comments/1q2449l/microsofts_satya_nadella_wants_you_to_stop_saying/
stitchPrompt: Design an analytical brand-safety product called AI Ad Adjacency Shield for performance marketers, media buyers, creator partnership managers, agencies, and brand-safety leads placing spend across short-form video, newsletters, and creator feeds. Users should enter campaign, creator/channel list, audience fit, example posts, unsafe keywords, AI-content signals, spend at risk, and approval rules, then score suitability, flag risky AI-slop adjacency, compare creator context, and create a buy/hold/review decision memo. Include a campaign risk intake, creator and channel suitability matrix, AI slop adjacency scanner, unsafe context keyword rail, spend-at-risk forecast, buy/hold/review decision queue, and brand-safety memo export. Design direction: use a financial-analyst aesthetic with institutional ink/navy surfaces, muted risk heatmaps, confidence bands, compact comparison tables, and sober decision memos so the product feels like a premium media-risk workbench, not a social listening toy.
